report_text:
Topic 10 (slides 140‑146) focuses almost exclusively on Dockerfile syntax and the mechanics of image layers. The slide text explains how a Dockerfile is distributed, built, and how each instruction creates a layer, and it briefly mentions incremental rebuilds. This content addresses several of the matched questions—particularly those about Dockerfile, image layers, and why multiple containers can share the same image.

However, the other questions in the matched set are not answered within this slide range. Topics such as Docker namespaces, UnionFS, what containers share with the host OS, the role of the Docker daemon, the distinction between images and containers, Docker registries, and the broader benefits of Docker are all absent from slides 140‑146. A search of the deck shows that these concepts appear in adjacent or later topics: namespaces are covered in slides 152‑153, UnionFS in slides 178‑181, the Docker daemon in slides 137‑138, and registries in slide 147. Thus the omission is not a deck‑wide gap but a shallow coverage within this particular topic.

Recommendation: Add a concise summary of the missing concepts to the end of the Dockerfile/layers section or create a short bridging slide that references the relevant slides (152‑153 for namespaces, 178‑181 for UnionFS, 137‑138 for the daemon, 147 for registries). This will give students a more complete picture of Docker’s architecture without requiring them to jump to unrelated topics.
